# Hypotheses H6 to H12: outcomes

Version 2 set out seven hypotheses before the work began (build2 Section 14), each with the test that would falsify it. Each is reported here as supported, partly supported, not supported or not yet tested, with the evidence. Every number is filled from a results file.

## H6: the box-to-ground step causes most of the extra range error on detected objects

*Hypothesis:* end-to-end range error on detected objects is larger than ground-pixel range error mainly because of the box-to-ground step, and the Phase 9 footprint fix removes most of the difference.

**Supported, for vehicles.** With exact poses (SynDrone), ranging a ground pixel is exact, so any systematic error on a detected vehicle comes from choosing its ground point. Ranging the bottom edge of the box read vehicles short: median signed error -0.7% pooled, -2.4% at 20 m (development towns, version 1's tracks). Ranging to the footprint centre (D-736) and then to the contact point (D-743) brought it to +0.2% (+0.1% at 20 m), the median absolute error from 1.1% to 0.4%, and the 90th percentile from 4.0% to 2.3%. The contact point was fitted on these towns, so its step was tested on the calibration towns: median absolute error 0.7% to 0.5% with version 1's detector, 0.6% to 0.4% with version 2's. On the test towns, run once, vehicles' median error is 0.4%. People needed no correction: a standing person's box already ends at the feet, and moving it made them worse (D-736). Not tested: real footage with known distances, where pose error, not the box, is likely to dominate.

## H7: speeds shown only when the filter is confident are accurate and calibrated

*Hypothesis:* speeds shown only when the filter is confident are accurate to the stated tolerance, and their intervals are calibrated.

**Not supported.** No display rule reached the target (9 in 10 shown speeds within tolerance, at least 100 shown) on the development towns with the version 2 detector: the best rule for people was right 74% of the time, for vehicles 84% (D-739, D-740). So, as fixed before the test, the pipeline shows no speeds, and the one-time test could not score displayed speeds. The intervals themselves were calibrated (conformal, D-737), but a calibrated interval does not single out the speeds that are wrong. With version 1's detector a person rule came close (89%, D-739), so a more precise person detector is the likeliest route.

## H8: conditional calibration brings each group's coverage close to nominal

*Hypothesis:* conditional calibration brings coverage within each group to within a few points of nominal, where the single scalar did not.

**Partly supported.** On the SynDrone test towns, calibrated on other towns and run once, range intervals at nominal 68 / 90 / 95 % held 78% / 95% / 97% for people and 76% / 93% / 97% for vehicles: within a few points at 90 and 95 %, about ten points too wide at 68 %. Leave-one-flight-out, the conditional (Mondrian) method beat version 1's single factor clearly, but still missed nominal by 8 to 10 points on average per cell and held-out flight (D-737): flights differ more than any grouping by angle, range and class captures. On Mid-Air, with fused poses, the filter's own covariance gave 87% / 91% / 92% at the same levels. The SynDrone calibration holds for exact poses only; with navigation errors added the 90 % intervals held far less (docs/syndrone_eval.md), so they must be refitted for the navigation flown.

## H9: camera, IMU and GPS fusion brings range error close to the exact-pose result

*Hypothesis:* tightly coupled camera, IMU and GPS fusion brings ranging error with realistic navigation close to the exact-pose result.

**Supported.** On the Mid-Air test flights, run once, median range error was 4.5% with fused poses against 3.1% with exact poses, and 7.3% / 13.8% / 38.7% under version 1's assumed good, typical and poor navigation (D-741). Fusion recovers most of the gap between assumed typical navigation and exact poses. The filter was not fully consistent: its normalised error for all states was above the expected band, driven by a GPS burst the filter took in ungated; a GPS gate was added afterwards and checked on development flights only (D-744). Mid-Air flights are synthetic, so real sensors may do worse.

## H10: a permissive detector and the project's tracker match or beat the Ultralytics stack

*Hypothesis:* a permissively licensed detector and our own tracker match or beat the Ultralytics stack on VisDrone.

**Partly supported.** On VisDrone test-dev, run once, identity F1 was 0.692 for vehicles and 0.321 for people, against 0.760 and 0.436 for version 1 (which ran at 960 pixels; D-730). It does not match on tracking. It does beat version 1 on small-object detection: 38% of people 16 to 32 pixels tall detected, against 27%; but only 6% are kept by a track, because the tracker starts tracks only at high scores, which small people rarely reach (D-730, D-733). The licence goal is met: no AGPL code runs in version 2 (D-725, D-732).

## H11: the pipeline fits a Raspberry Pi 5 at a useful rate for search

*Hypothesis:* the pipeline fits a Raspberry Pi 5 at a useful rate for search.

**Not yet tested.** No Pi 5 has been available, so the detector's time on one is estimated, not measured: about 285 ms per frame for D-FINE N at 640 (0.75 to 1.5 times that, D-723), so detection about every 0.3 s. The rate a search needs was left to be set from the search pattern's speed and image overlap; the Phase 14 measurement now bears on it: at SynDrone's 21.9 m/s and 25 frames per second, a person's chance of being detected in a pass rose steeply with the number of frames they stayed in view (docs/multi_drone.md), so detecting on fewer frames is expected to cost detections, not only latency. `make pi-benchmark` gives the measurement when a device exists.

## H12: sharing observations between drones speeds up search and degrades gracefully

*Hypothesis:* sharing observations between drones reduces time to find and repeated coverage compared with independent search, and degrades gracefully with packet loss.

**Partly supported.** In the Phase 14 simulation, run once on test seeds with the camera measured on SynDrone, sharing beat the same planner without sharing at every team size (four drones: mean time to find 1,065 s against 1,464 s), repeated slightly less ground (90% of passes against 93%), and degraded gracefully: at 90 % packet loss it fell back to no-sharing time (1,458 s), never below it. With too little bandwidth it did not degrade gracefully: below the bytes sharing produces, its advantage soon disappeared (development seeds, after a fault in the test's budget model was found; D-756). Against the other baseline, independent lawnmower strips, it lost at every team size (four drones: lawnmower 645 s), because the detector's false alarms pull map-guided drones back to check them. Details and the byte-budget follow-up: [docs/multi_drone.md](multi_drone.md).
